scams.name: Dotonbori Cabaret Bar Cover Charge
scams.avoidance: Never enter a bar because someone outside is specifically recruiting you Always ask for an English menu with all charges listed before ordering anything Look up bars on Google Maps or Tabelog before entering rather than following touts
scams.location: Cabaret and hostess bars around Dotonbori and Namba

scams.name: 'Marc the Beggar' Loan Scam
scams.avoidance: This specific individual is well-documented — search 'Marc Japan scam' for photos Never lend cash to strangers regardless of how convincing the story Genuine emergencies can be handled by the nearest police box (koban)
scams.location: Tourist areas citywide, reported near Shinsaibashi

scams.name: Coin Change Shortchange
scams.avoidance: Familiarize yourself with yen coin sizes and values before shopping Count your coins in front of the cashier — this is socially acceptable in Japan Use IC cards (Suica, ICOCA) for transit and cashless payment where possible
scams.location: Touristy shops and market stalls, especially in Namba

scams.name: Fake Charity Clipboard
scams.avoidance: Legitimate Japanese charities do not solicit cash donations on the street Decline politely and keep walking — 'daijōbu desu' (I'm fine, thanks) works If you want to donate to disaster relief, use official NGO websites
scams.location: Shinsaibashi shopping street and busy tourist areas

scams.name: Overpriced Tourist Lunch Menus
scams.avoidance: Walk five minutes away from any major sight before choosing a restaurant Use Google Maps to find highly-rated restaurants in the surrounding area Osaka's covered shopping arcades (Tenjinbashisuji, etc.) have excellent cheap food far from tourist premiums
scams.location: Restaurants directly adjacent to Osaka Castle and Universal Studios

scams.name: Counterfeit Brand Goods in Shinsaibashi
scams.avoidance: If a price seems too good to be true for a luxury brand, it's counterfeit Buy branded goods only from official stores or major department stores like Isetan or Hankyu Importing counterfeit goods back to most countries is a customs offense

scams.name: The Post-Expo 2025 Ticket and Myaku-Myaku Merchandise Fraud
scams.avoidance: Expo 2025 closed in October 2025—any site selling 'Expo tickets' in 2026 is a scam. Buy Myaku-Myaku merchandise only from official licensees (Osaka Tourism Bureau shops and major department stores such as Hankyu, Daimaru, or Takashimaya). Never click Expo-themed ads on social media. If you've already paid a suspicious site, file a chargeback with your card issuer within 60 days and report the site to the Consumer Affairs Agency hotline on 188.
scams.location: Online with in-person pickup/ticket-swap attempts near Yumeshima Expo site and Osaka Station

scams.name: The Dotonbori Pickpocket and Phone-Hold Distraction
scams.avoidance: Wear a cross-body bag with zipper forward or money belt under clothes. Never put valuables in back or open jacket pockets. At Glico Bridge, stand with back to wall, not in crowd center. Don't hand your phone to strangers—ask uniformed staff instead. On Midosuji Line during rush hour, wear backpack on front.
scams.location: Dotonbori crowds, Namba Walk, Shin-Osaka Shinkansen platforms, Osaka Metro Midosuji Line rush hour, Nara Park
